name: Transformers
title: How Hugging Face Transformers Runs a Model: pipeline() | Language Lineage
h1: What Actually Happens When You Run a Hugging Face Pipeline?
description: Trace a Hugging Face Transformers text-generation pipeline: Rust tokenizer, safetensors weights, PyTorch model, generate(), SDPA attention on CPU, CUDA or Apple MPS, with sources.
og_subtitle: pipeline() → Rust tokenizer → PyTorch model → generate() → SDPA → CPU · CUDA · MPS
verified_against: the Transformers documentation (Pipeline tutorial, Pipelines reference, Loading models, Tokenizers, Attention backends, Generation strategies) and the PyTorch MPS backend notes
scope: Documented path for one text-generation pipeline() call with the PyTorch backend, default greedy decoding and the default SDPA attention, on a CPU, an NVIDIA GPU or an Apple silicon GPU. Other tasks, other attention implementations (FlashAttention, paged attention), quantization, multi-GPU placement with device_map, Accelerate and other frameworks are out of scope. What happens inside PyTorch on each device is on the PyTorch page.
answer: A **pipeline()** call runs four documented stages: **tokenization**, **model inference**, **post-processing** and output. The tokenizer turns text into token ids with Hugging Face's **Rust** tokenizers library. The model is a **PyTorch** module whose weights **from_pretrained()** loads from **safetensors** files when they exist. **generate()** then calls the model one step at a time, by default greedily keeping the most likely next token, up to 20 new tokens unless the model's config says otherwise. Attention runs through PyTorch's **SDPA**, which picks the fastest kernel on a CUDA GPU and the C++ implementation on the CPU; on Apple silicon the operations run as MPS kernels. The output ids are decoded back into text.

sections.heading: Which device it picks
paragraphs: If you do not pass a device, the pipeline places the model on the first accelerator it finds (a CUDA GPU, Apple silicon's MPS, or others) and uses the CPU only when there is none. Passing device="cpu" or device="mps" forces a choice.

sections.heading: Where Python hands off
paragraphs: Most of the work in this path is not Python: tokenization runs in Rust, and the model's layers run as PyTorch kernels. For what PyTorch does with those operations on each device, see [what happens when you run a PyTorch model](/ai/how-pytorch-runs). For serving many requests at once, engines such as [vLLM](/ai/how-vllm-runs) add batching schedulers and KV-cache management on top of the same kind of model.

stages.name: Your pipeline() call
stages.summary: Python code such as pipeline(task="text-generation", model=...), which picks a default model and preprocessor for the task unless you name one.

evidence.quote: Each task is configured to use a default pretrained model and preprocessor, but this can be overridden with the model parameter if you want to use a different model.

stages.name: Pipeline
stages.summary: Transformers' Pipeline class: tokenization, model inference and post-processing in one call, on the device it chooses or you set.

evidence.quote: Pipeline workflow is defined as a sequence of the following operations: Input -> Tokenization -> Model Inference -> Post-Processing (task dependent) -> Output

stages.name: safetensors weights
stages.summary: The model's configuration and weights from the Hugging Face Hub or a local folder, read from safetensors files when they exist.

evidence.quote: The from_pretrained() method loads weights stored in the safetensors file format if they’re available.

stages.name: Tokenizer (Rust core)
stages.summary: Turns text into token ids. Fast tokenizers run on the Rust tokenizers library, which parallelizes batches across threads.

evidence.quote: TokenizersBackend handles large batches faster because its Rust-based backend parallelizes work across threads.

stages.name: PyTorch model
stages.summary: The model class (for text generation, a causal language model) holding the loaded weights on the chosen device.

evidence.quote: It requires a model class and the from_pretrained() method.

stages.name: generate() loop
stages.summary: Produces new tokens one step at a time by calling the model; by default it is greedy search, up to 20 new tokens unless the model's generation config says otherwise.

evidence.quote: Greedy search is the default decoding strategy. It selects the next most likely token at each step.
Unless specified in GenerationConfig , this strategy generates a maximum of 20 new tokens.

stages.name: Post-processing
stages.summary: Turns the output token ids back into text for the result.

evidence.quote: Postprocess will receive the raw outputs of the _forward method, generally tensors, and reformat them into something more friendly.

stages.name: PyTorch SDPA
stages.summary: Transformers' default attention function: PyTorch's scaled dot product attention.

evidence.quote: Omit certain backbones from the dict to use the default attention function (SDPA).

stages.name: C++ attention
stages.summary: On backends other than CUDA, SDPA uses PyTorch's C++ implementation.

evidence.quote: It defaults to the PyTorch C++ implementation for other backends.

stages.name: MPS kernels
stages.summary: On the mps device, PyTorch runs operations as Metal Performance Shaders graphs and kernels.

evidence.quote: It introduces a new device to map Machine Learning computational graphs and primitives on highly efficient Metal Performance Shaders Graph framework and tuned kernels provided by Metal Performance Shaders framework respectively.

stages.name: Fastest CUDA kernel
stages.summary: On CUDA, SDPA automatically picks the fastest available attention kernel.

evidence.quote: PyTorch’s scaled dot product attention (SDPA) selects the fastest attention function for CUDA backends automatically.

stages.name: CPU
stages.summary: Used only when no accelerator is available, or when you pass device="cpu".

evidence.quote: By default, when device is left unset, Pipeline automatically places the model on the first available accelerator (CUDA GPU, Apple Silicon MPS, XPU, …) and only falls back to a CPU when none is available.

stages.name: Apple silicon GPU
stages.summary: The GPU of an Apple silicon Mac, through PyTorch's mps device.

evidence.quote: To run Pipeline on Apple silicon, set device="mps".

stages.name: NVIDIA GPU
stages.summary: The first choice when device is left unset and a CUDA GPU is present.

evidence.quote: By default, when device is left unset, Pipeline automatically places the model on the first available accelerator (CUDA GPU, Apple Silicon MPS, XPU, …) and only falls back to a CPU when none is available.
